Passed checks:
- CSV shape is 19 data rows x 5 columns; draft/curation JSON parse cleanly.
- source_count=1 and source_urls length=1, pointing to https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_epidemics_and_pandemics.
- The registered source has the relevant table titled "Epidemics and pandemics with at least 1 million deaths" and states the ranking convention for averaging death-toll ranges (source: registered Wikipedia master, By death toll section, lines 149-150 in fetched text).
- Schema matches the pre-staging ruling: Event PK, Disease, Death Toll, Years, Location; Death Toll is categorical text, no Percentage column.
- 19-row universe is correct under the master display: rank 1 has two displayed rows, then ranks 2-18 have one each (source: registered Wikipedia master, By death toll table, lines 151-169).
- Sort preserves master display order, including Plague of Justinian before 1918 Spanish flu at the top.
- HIV/AIDS and COVID-19 preserve the staged "(as of 2026)" qualifier, and source-defined claim_type is defensible.

Finding 1 - Several cells are not master-verbatim despite the declared verbatim rule. (factual, BLOCKING)
Evidence from the registered source set: the master table displays Plague of Justinian location as "North Africa, Europe, and Western Asia" (By death toll table, line 151), but the CSV has "North Africa, Europe, Western Asia". It displays Black Death location as "Europe, Asia, and North Africa" (line 153), but the CSV has "Europe, Asia, North Africa". It displays the rank-6 event as "Cocoliztli epidemic of 1545–1548" and disease as "Cocoliztli, caused by an unidentified pathogen" (line 157), but the CSV has "Cocoliztli epidemic 1545–1548" and "Cocoliztli (unidentified pathogen)". It displays Antonine Plague years as "165–180 (possibly up to 190)" (line 158), but the CSV has "165–180".

Why it matters: draft.json::temporal_note and curation.json::normalization_decisions repeatedly assert Event, Disease, Years, and Location are source-verbatim. These discrepancies affect row-value grounding in the registered master, not just prose. The Event mismatch also touches the PK.

Minimal fix: update the CSV and matching curation universe_listing / normalization examples to the master-displayed values, or explicitly reframe these fields as normalized text and document the normalization rule. Preferred repair is source-verbatim update because that is the stated policy and keeps source_count=1 clean.

Wiki-family discovery pass: no more direct Wikipedia page appears necessary for this query. The staged master is the direct list/table source for epidemics and pandemics by death toll, and sibling broad death-toll/disaster pages are less specific than the registered source.

Minimal follow-up fixes:
1. Correct the affected CSV cells to source-displayed values: the two Location cells, the Cocoliztli 1545–1548 Event and Disease cells, and Antonine Plague Years.
2. Refresh curation.json universe_listing and normalization_decisions examples to match the repaired cells.
3. Keep the current source_count=1, 19-row universe, sort, schema, claim_type, domain, and entity-class metadata unchanged.

Verdict: Not ready until the source-verbatim cell mismatches are repaired.
